claims.text: Male infant vaccinated with BCG on November 29, 2022 who developed sudden bouts of high fever (38°C) on March 29, 2023, with decreased humoral immunity and zero T and NK cell counts on April 4, 2023. Genetic analysis on April 11, 2023 revealed JAK3-associated SCID (two JAK3 missense variants) and NGS on April 12, 2023 showed Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex group infection.

Genetic analysis on April 11, 2023 revealed that the infant had JAK3-associated severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID).

There were two heterozygous mutations in the JAK3 gene: (1) c.308 G > A (exon 3, NM_000215.4) led to a change in the amino acid p.Arg103His, which was a missense mutation. According to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) guidelines, the variant was determined to be a suspected pathogenic variant PM1+PP3+PM3_Strong+PM2_Supporting.

(2) c.307C > T (exon 3, NM_000215.4) led to a change in the amino acid p.Arg103Cys, which was a missense mutation. According to the ACMG guidelines, the variant was determined to be a suspected pathogenic variant PM1+PP3+PM3_Strong+PM2_Supporting.
Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex group infection was observed via next-generation sequencing (NGS) on April 12, 2023.

claims.text: He was treated with anti-tuberculosis drugs (rifampicin, isoniazid, linezolid, with linezolid changed to oral after five days), received HSCT on July 11, 2023, and had isoniazid and linezolid long term. The injection-site abscess burst in April 2023 and sore cleaning with suture surgery was done on June 21, 2023. He recovered well. The causal association with BCG vaccination was inconclusive but could not be disregarded.
